question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Goa — Location & Capture]
options: Goa is located on the western coast of India
Goa was captured by the Portuguese under Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510
Goa was seized from the Adil Shahi Sultan of Bijapur
Goa is situated at the mouth of the Mahanadi River
wrong_fact: Goa is NOT situated at the mouth of the Mahanadi River. It lies on the Konkan coast between the Mandovi and Zuari rivers. The Mahanadi is an east-coast river (Odisha/Chhattisgarh) with no connection to Goa.
explanation: Goa sits on India's western (Konkan) coast, flanked by the Mandovi (Mahadayi) and Zuari rivers. Afonso de Albuquerque captured it in 1510 from Yusuf Adil Shah of Bijapur, making it the headquarters of the Portuguese Estado da India. The Mahanadi empties into the Bay of Bengal near Cuttack/Paradip — entirely unrelated to Goa.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Goa — Neighbouring Regions & Colonial Context]
options: Goa shares its northern border with Maharashtra
Goa shares its eastern and southern borders with Karnataka
The Portuguese used Goa as the administrative capital of their eastern empire
Goa was the first territory captured by the Portuguese on the Indian subcontinent
wrong_fact: Goa was NOT the first territory captured by the Portuguese on the Indian subcontinent. Cochin (Kochi) and Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast had earlier Portuguese footholds (factories and forts). Goa was captured in 1510, whereas Portuguese contact with India began with Vasco da Gama's arrival at Calicut in 1498.
explanation: Goa does border Maharashtra to the north and Karnataka to the south and east. It served as the capital of the Estado da India. However, the Portuguese first established a factory at Calicut (1498) and a fort at Cochin (1503) before taking Goa in 1510. So Goa was a crucial acquisition but not the chronologically first foothold.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Goa — Strategic Importance & Trade Routes]
options: Goa's natural harbour on the Mandovi River made it ideal for controlling Arabian Sea trade
Goa served as a transit hub for the spice trade from the Malabar Coast to Portugal via the Cape of Good Hope route
The Portuguese Inquisition was established at Goa in 1560 to enforce Christianity among converts
Goa was strategically located to dominate the overland Silk Road connecting India to China
wrong_fact: Goa had no strategic relevance to the overland Silk Road, which ran through Central Asia (Samarkand, Bukhara) connecting China to the Mediterranean. Goa's strategic value lay in controlling the SEA ROUTE — the Arabian Sea maritime trade linking India's spice-rich Malabar Coast to Europe via the Cape of Good Hope.
explanation: The natural deep-water harbour of the Mandovi at Goa allowed the Portuguese to interdict and control Arabian Sea trade, displacing Arab and Gujarat merchants. The Cape Route bypassed Ottoman-controlled overland routes. The Goa Inquisition (1560) persecuted converts who secretly continued Hindu/Muslim practices. None of these relate to the Silk Road, which was a Central Asian land route entirely outside Portuguese reach.
